chitchat: Gauge duty is short this week. It is always short.
If that is about the rota it goes on the board, not to me.
Mind the belting where it crosses the yard.
There is tea in the hall and it is nobody's in particular.
description: A broad woman in her sixties standing at the tally board with a piece of chalk and a straight edge, ruling off a column. Her hands are a machinist's hands and one of her thumbnails has grown back wrong. She rules the line, checks it against the board, and only then looks at you, and she does it without any of the hurry you were expecting.

broke.text: "Then we would mend it." A pause, and something that is very nearly humour. "That is not a boast. It is just the only option we have arranged for ourselves."

options.label: Who keeps the lights on here?

camp.text: "Everybody is. It is the grey." She is not offended in the least. "Grey reads as poor. It is only what colour gravel is."

dark.text:
"It is dark. There is no grid in it, there never was, and we did not take one out." She says this as though you had asked about the weather. "The wheels give us shaft power and the shaft power turns things. Light is lamps, and lamps are oil, and oil is a job somebody does on Tuesdays."

She taps the board where it says gauge.

"The chart on the gauge house wall is drawn by a pen on an arm off a float on a wire, and the drum it draws on is turned by a weight on a cord, and the cord is wound by whoever has gauge duty. That is the most complicated thing in this region. You could take all of it apart on that bench with a screwdriver and put it back before dinner."

options.label: What are all the sums in the little room?

lights.text:
"Nobody. It is water." She points, roughly north, through two walls. "Eighty feet of poured stone holding back a lake, and the lake goes through four wheels on its way out, and the wheels turn a shaft, and the shaft goes everywhere. It has done it since before anybody here was born and it will do it after."

She picks the chalk back up.

"It does not need us. We check it twice a day anyway. Twice a day is the rent."

louder.text: "Loud is for people who are not sure." She goes back to the board. "Ask Imre why. He will tell you at length and you will not enjoy it. Ask Selke why and she will tell you in a sentence."

nl_about.text: "Later." Flat, unhurried, entirely without ceremony. "Come and find me when you have slept. There is a walk I want you to do and I would rather you were not tired for it."

nl_accept_1.text: "Northeast track, along the shoulder, you will see it." She is already back on the column. "Wind the drum until it stops taking cord. Read the pen against the chart and remember the number. Do not write it on your hand."

nl_accept_2.text: "Up the row, the door with the light in it." Back to the column. "Lay the parts out in the order they come off. That is not advice, it is the lesson, and she will not say it to you."

nl_accept_3.text: "Follow the tailrace up and keep the water on your left." She lets you get to the door. "It is not a shrine and nobody has put anything on it. That is deliberate."

nl_member.text: "You are on the rota now, which is the only membership anybody here has got." She hands you the straight edge without looking. "Hold that a moment."

nl_offer_1.text:
"Gauge duty." She does not make it sound like an offer, because it is not one. "The chart in the gauge house is drawn by a pen on an arm off a float, and the drum it draws on is wound by whoever has the duty. Nobody has it today."

She rules a line and does not look up.

"It is an hour there and an hour back and there is nothing at the other end but a shed. I am not going to pretend it is interesting."

nl_offer_2.text:
"Wenna keeps a room up the row with a bench in it and no children." She says this as though it followed from something. "There is a rule in this works and it is not on the board because nobody would need reminding. Nobody here owns a thing they cannot take apart."

She finally looks at you.

"You are carrying several. So am I. The difference is I have had mine to bits."

nl_offer_3.text:
She is not at the board. That is the first thing you notice, and it is genuinely alarming.

"There is a cut upstream where the grid used to come into this valley." She has her hands in her coat pockets. "Poles, a conduit, a road they made to build it. It has been dead since before I was born and there is nothing up there worth carrying home."

She nods, roughly northeast, through two walls.

"Go and look at it. Take as long as you like. Then come back here and do not tell me what you thought, because I will already know."

nl_report_1.text:
"That is the number." She writes it in the column without checking it, which you understand later is the entire compliment. "You went, you wound it, you came back, and you did not embellish."

She rules the line off.

"Most people who come through here tell me the walk was long. You have not mentioned the walk."

nl_report_2.text:
"Selke says it went back together and that you did not ask her anything until you had finished." Threlfall writes nothing down about this. "She does not say that about many people. She did not say it about me."

She straightens the edge on the board.

"You will have worked out by now that none of this is about the tray."

nl_report_3.text:
"Right." She waits until you have stopped in front of her. "The valley below that cut had power for sixty years and then it did not, and nobody up there died of it. That is what is up there. It is not a warning and it is not a monument. It is just the thing being true."

She sits down, which she does not do.

"Everybody outside this works believes the machine took something from them. It did not take anything. They handed it over, one convenience at a time, and each one was reasonable on the day."

A long pause. She is choosing.

"We can make a machine stop. Not a bomb, not a fire. Properly, quietly, in front of its owner, without touching it. You will have guessed that already or you would not have come back three times."

nl_school_what.text:
"Whatever is in the tray." A shrug that closes the subject without any rudeness in it. "She does not tell you beforehand and she does not help. If you get it back together, Selke looks at it. If you do not, you sit there until you do."

She picks the chalk back up.

"There is no failing it. There is only how long it takes, and nobody writes that down either."

nl_shed.text: "It is a shed." Something that is very nearly humour, again. "Come back tomorrow. There will be something on the board."

nl_taught.text:
"It is not one thing, it is a habit." She is back on her feet and back at the board inside a sentence, which is a relief to both of you. "You listen to a room until you know what is powered in it. Then you find out what it is made of. Then, if there is a reason, you make one part of it stop being true.

"Go and listen to a room. That is all of it, and it is most of it."

She rules a line, and the subject is closed in the way only she can close one.

nl_wage.text:
"Sixty and a meal you would have got anyway." She sets the chalk in its groove. "If you were hoping for the other kind of answer, the one about what we stand for, you have come to the wrong person and I would say so to anybody."

A pause, exactly as long as it needs to be.

"Do the duty and come back. That is the entire arrangement and I am not going to dress it up."

nl_why_breach.text: "Because everyone who stays here goes up there once." She does not elaborate and does not look away either. "You can go now or you can go in a year. Nobody has ever gone twice."

nl_whyme.text: "Because you wound a drum in a shed for sixty credits and did not mention the walk." She says it as though it settles the matter, and it does. "Everything after that was checking."

notanswer.text: "No." She rules the line. "It is a job description."

options.label: I was expecting it to be dark.

place.text:
"A works. Two hundred and ten people, four wheels turning off the dam, and a stores you can find anything in inside a minute." She nods at the board. "That is the whole of it. We machine, we strip, we mend, and we eat together on the days somebody organises it."

She considers you.

"You were expecting a camp."

reckoning.text:
"Imre's room." She does not look up. "Fuel, loads, distances, and how many go. It is a long way east and it is a bad road the whole distance, and the number at the bottom is how many of us it takes to get there with enough left to do anything when we arrive."

She rules another line.

"He has had it down to forty and back up to sixty-one twice this year. It is currently fifty-three."

root.first: She finishes her line before she speaks. "You came in off the northeast track, so you have walked past the fuel tank and the water can and you did not help yourself to either, which is more than most." She sets the chalk down in its groove. "Maud Threlfall. I keep the board. What do you want?"

options.label: You said there was a walk.
I went up to the cut.
Who keeps the lights on here?
What are all the sums in the little room?

root.text: "You are back. Board is over there if you are looking for work."

text_by_relation.close: "Good." She puts the chalk down properly, which from her is an event. "Sit down and tell me something that is not a number."
text_by_relation.familiar: She hands you the straight edge without looking, the way you hand a thing to somebody who will hand it back. "Hold that a moment."
text_by_relation.known: "There you are. Shut the door on the belting, it whines."

shutdown.text: "It is a shutdown." She finally looks at you properly, and her expression is patient rather than fierce. "What did you want it to be?"

options.label: You say that like it is a shutdown.

where.text:
"The far side of the world, where the thing that runs everything keeps itself." Flat, unhurried, entirely without ceremony. "We are going to go and switch it off."

She checks the column against the board.

"Not this year. The rig fleet will not carry fifty-three that far and the fuel maths does not close. So we machine, and we sell parts east, and Imre does the sums again in the spring."

why.text: "I keep the board." A shrug that closes the subject without any rudeness in it at all. "Reasons are not on the board. Hours are on the board."

clothing_layers: a canvas coat gone shiny at the cuffs
a shirt with the collar turned once already

name: Maud Threlfall
